subject: Contract: incident response timelines, evidence handover, and subprocessors — FinServe follow-up
messages:
From: Alison Park <alison.park@finserve.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.inference>
Cc: Tom Briggs <t.briggs@finserve.com>
Date: 2028-04-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Clarify incident timelines & evidence handover — contract question

Hi Irene,

Thanks again for walking us through the platform yesterday. As we're progressing the DPA review internally, Security and Procurement have a couple of concrete asks around incident notification and evidence handover that need contractual confirmation before we can finalize the PO. High-level:

- What is Redwood's committed timeline to notify customers of a confirmed data security incident? (we asked for SLA windows)
- In the event we request forensic artifacts (pcap, extracted logs, snapshots of affected KV cache), how quickly can Redwood provide an export / transfer and under what access model?
- Can you confirm how Redwood treats access to subprocessor logs and whether customers can require Redwood to obtain and deliver subprocessor evidence?

I've attached our Security Questionnaire (excerpt) that highlights the sections. Procurement would also like to see a short Mutual Action Plan (MOP) so we can timeline internal approvals.

Can you outline proposed contractual language and an execution plan? We're trying to avoid protracted redlines on timeline items.

Best,
Alison Park
Head of Security Programs | FinServe, Inc.
alison.park@finserve.com
+1 415 555 3290

Attachment: FinServe_SecQuestionnaire_2028.pdf

From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.inference>
To: Alison Park <alison.park@finserve.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.inference>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.inference>, PrIyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.inference>
Date: 2028-04-18T10:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify incident timelines & evidence handover — contract question

Alison —

Appreciate the clear asks. High-level answers up front, then a suggested operational cadence and the documents we'll attach for legal:

1) Notification windows
   - Acknowledge receipt of suspected incident: within 4 hours of detection/confirmation internal to Redwood.
   - Initial customer notification (high-level): within 48 hours of confirmation of a security incident that materially affects customer data.
   - Detailed incident report (preliminary findings): usually within 7 calendar days, with subsequent updates as new facts emerge.
   - Final forensics + root cause: targeted within 30 calendar days, subject to the scope of third-party involvement.

2) Evidence handover model
   - For routine artifact requests (logs, KV snapshots, request traces): we will export and deliver via encrypted SFTP or secure transfer link. Standard target: delivery initiation within 7 calendar days of written evidence request, complete handover typically within 14 calendar days depending on volume and redaction needs.
   - For large-scale forensic exports or raw packet captures: we require a mutually agreed MOP and may use an escrowed transfer or third-party forensic custodian. Delivery windows for these items are scoped per-incident.

3) Subprocessor access and evidence
   - Redwood maintains a subprocessor roster and agrees to notify customers of material changes per the DPA.
   - If evidence resides with a subprocessor, Redwood will use contractual levers to obtain and deliver the requested artifacts. We can commit to best-effort delivery within the same evidence timelines above, but must explicitly reserve time for subprocessor cooperation and any legal export controls.

Operational ask: Can FinServe accept the 48-hour initial notification + 7/14/30 day evidence cadence above? If you need a stricter 24-hour guarantee for initial notification or a hard SLA for subprocessor artifacts, flag that now so we can route to Legal/Contracts for a waiver or alternative wording.

Attaching: Redwood's incident response template (redwood_incident_response_template.docx) and a current subprocessor snapshot (subprocessor_chain_v1.csv) — those should help with clause drafting.

I'll loop in PrIyom on the ops handoffs (SFTP, access logs) and Ben for subprocessor coordination. Marissa will propose contract language.

Thanks,
Irene Choi
Head, Privacy & Compliance | Redwood Inference
irene.choi@redwood.inference

Attachments: redwood_incident_response_template.docx; subprocessor_chain_v1.csv

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.inference>
To: Alison Park <alison.park@finserve.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.inference>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.inference>
Date: 2028-04-18T11:23:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify incident timelines & evidence handover — contract question

Alison/Irene —

Quick operational clarifications from the subprocessor/team side:

- Subprocessor chain: the attached CSV lists current subprocessors and materiality notes. For anything we categorize as "material subprocessor" (e.g., managed storage, telemetry aggregators), we have standing agreements that require cooperation on security events.
- Evidence retrieval: when artifacts live with a subprocessor, Redwood triggers our escalation playbook which includes an executive SLA breach call with that vendor. Realistically, that adds 48–96 hours of coordination beyond our internal timelines in cases where vendor cooperation is required. We document those delays in the incident timeline we provide customers.
- Auditability: we can provide an access log archive (ISO timestamps + request IDs) with any evidence delivery. If FinServe needs a signed chain-of-custody, we should scope that as part of the MOP.

If you want, we can include a short sentence in the DPA acknowledging that subprocessor-sourced artifacts are "subject to vendor cooperation" and that Redwood will pursue delivery but cannot guarantee vendor turnaround times beyond best efforts. Happy to include stronger guarantees if Legal approves an indemnity clause — that's typically the tradeoff.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Director of Security Operations | Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.inference>
To: Alison Park <alison.park@finserve.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.inference>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.inference>, PrIyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.inference>
Date: 2028-04-18T13:17:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify incident timelines & evidence handover — contract question

Alison —

Thanks — see the attached redline (proposed_incident_clause_redline.pdf). Summary of proposed contractual language:

- Initial notification: Redwood will provide initial written notice to the customer within forty‑eight (48) hours of confirmation of a security incident affecting customer data.
- Evidence delivery: Redwood will use commercially reasonable efforts to provide requested forensic artifacts within fourteen (14) calendar days of a written request; for artifacts held by subprocessors Redwood will use contractual remedies to obtain and deliver such artifacts and will provide the customer with a documented timeline of any third‑party delays.
- Cross‑border transfers: Redwood will not transfer evidence outside the EU/UK/US jurisdictions without prior written consent; where cross‑border movement is necessary, Redwood will identify the legal basis (e.g., SCCs, adequacy) and provide redacted summaries until consent is obtained.

I've softened absolute SLA guarantees around subprocessor cooperation into "commercially reasonable efforts" and included a requirement for a documented delay timeline. If FinServe requires a firm SLA for subprocessor artifacts, we'll need to agree scope/indemnity and possibly an escrow/forensics custodian arrangement.

Open to redlines — flagged the cross‑border sentence because I think that's where Procurement will press.

Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Privacy | Redwood Inference
Attachment: proposed_incident_clause_redline.pdf

From: Tom Briggs <t.briggs@finserve.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.inference>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.inference>
Cc: Alison Park <alison.park@finserve.com>, PrIyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.inference>
Date: 2028-04-18T15:43:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify incident timelines & evidence handover — contract question

Marissa / Irene —

Thanks for the rapid responses and the redline. Procurement and Security are largely aligned on the 48/7/14/30 operational cadence — that works for our internal SLA gating, provided we get explicit language on:

1) Cross‑border evidence movement: we need a clause that requires Redwood to identify legal basis and seek written sign‑off from FinServe before transferring raw forensic artifacts out of EU/UK borders. Summaries can be shared by default, raw exports require explicit consent.
2) Subprocessor delay transparency: the proposed "documented timeline" is good; we also want an escalation contact and comms SLA for updates during the wait.

Can you produce a short two‑page MOP that lays out steps, owners, and target windows (for internal execs to accept quickly)? Also, please send the redline into DocuSign once both sides agree to language to avoid email ping‑pong.

If you want, I can triage the final procurement language this afternoon.

Tom Briggs
Sr. Procurement Manager | FinServe, Inc.
